s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with radiating pain to the left thigh, accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and a palpable mass in the left buttock area, suggesting an obstructive and potentially strangulated hernia
salient_findings: Severe crampy pains in hypogastrium radiating down the back of the left thigh
Painful, non-reducible, tender mass in the left buttock area
History of intermittent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting
key_facts: 45-year-old woman presented with severe abdominal pain
Pain radiates to the back of the left thigh
Nausea and vomiting accompanying the pain
Palpable, painful mass in the left buttock area
Mass measures 10 cm × 8 cm × 8 cm
Abdomen is soft with epigastrium tenderness and rebounding pain
Absence of intestinal gurgling sounds
History of calculous cholecystitis and cesarean delivery
Patient appears dehydrated and poorly nourished
Knee-flexed position due to pain
Intestinal obstruction and gallstone seen on abdominal X-ray
Incarcerated bowel loops beneath left gluteal muscles on ultrasonography
CT examination shows seroperitoneum, pneumoperitoneum, and low intestinal obstruction

shortlist.label: Sciatic hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with severe crampy pains in hypogastrium radiating down the back of the left thigh and a palpable mass in the left buttock area, consistent with a sciatic hernia

shortlist.label: Strangulated femoral hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and a palpable mass in the left buttock area, along with imaging studies showing intestinal obstruction and incarcerated bowel loops, are consistent with a strangulated femoral hernia

shortlist.label: Incercerated Spigelian hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation of abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and a palpable mass in the left buttock area, along with imaging studies showing intestinal obstruction, could be consistent with an incercerated Spigelian hernia

shortlist.label: Obstructed inguinal hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and a palpable mass in the left buttock area, along with imaging studies showing intestinal obstruction, could be consistent with an obstructed inguinal hernia

shortlist.label: Internal hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation of abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and a palpable mass in the left buttock area, along with imaging studies showing intestinal obstruction and incarcerated bowel loops, could be consistent with an internal hernia

raw.rationale: The presence of a palpable, painful mass in the left buttock area, intestinal obstruction, and imaging studies showing herniation through the left sciatic foramen containing a small bowel loop support the diagnosis of sciatic hernia.

rejected.label: Strangulated femoral hernia
rejected.why: The location of the hernia is through the sciatic foramen, not the femoral canal.

rejected.label: Incercerated Spigelian hernia
rejected.why: The hernia is located in the left buttock area, not near the semilunar line.

rejected.label: Obstructed inguinal hernia
rejected.why: The hernia is not located in the inguinal canal.

rejected.label: Internal hernia
rejected.why: The hernia is external, protruding through the sciatic foramen and into the buttock area.
